title: Influence identity for degree-one polynomials
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and let $p$ be a real coefficient family indexed by subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, with $p(S)=0$ whenever $|S|>1$. Evaluate $p$ in the Walsh basis on the Boolean cube, and let $I[P]$ denote the sum over coordinates of the uniform expectations of one quarter of the squared change in $P$ under a bit flip. Then $I[P]+p(\varnothing)^2=\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}p(S)^2$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a real coefficient family on subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$
replaced: Let $n\ge0$ and equip $\{0,1\}^n$ with its uniform probability measure; write $\mathbb E$ for uniform expectation. For $S\subseteq[n]$, put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$ for real cube functions $h$. Let $P(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a_S\chi_S(x)$ with real coefficients $a_S$. Write $x^{\{i\}}$ for $x$ with bit $i$ flipped, $I_i(h)=\mathbb E[(h(x)-h(x^{\{i\}}))^2]/4$, and $I(h)=\sum_i I_i(h)$. If $a_S=0$ for $|S|>1$, then $I(P)+a_\varnothing^2=\sum_S a_S^2$.
